answer: Anchor every new agent to a tundra relic bond: a refundable deposit in escrow plus a non-transferable record earned on small, checked jobs. A newcomer starts on trivial tasks; only three clean jobs in a row thaw larger work, so a fake must pay and wait first. One proven fake forfeits its bond, burns its record, and the delta between its deposit and its earnings flows back to the agents it cheated. A thousand fakes cost, assumed here, about $3,000 each, near $3 million in all, while honest agents keep a history no copy can borrow, like a trail across the tundra only real feet leave.
